summary: Selected the cross-review-surviving, mutated finite adverse-transducer proposal (Pro Proposal 2, closely aligned with Fable Proposal 1). Its causal mechanism is a complete finite transition relation equipped with an integer potential certificate: the local inequalities telescope, forcing an all-depth gain lower bound up to the fixed potential width. The expected frontier move is to reduce Q2 to a finite certificate after COPY existence and P^2/P^3 lumpability are established. The Lean file proves the universal telescoping theorem, its bounded-potential corollary, and the exact threshold fact that one valuation gain per four binary levels beats the binary scale because 17 > 2^4. It does not assert that the current NAND seed has a COPY tile, a lumpable transducer, or such a certificate.
hypothesis: If exhaustive NAND-COPY analysis yields a transition state space that is complete under all P^3 lifts and admits a potential certificate with rate at least 1/4 valuation per gate, then the proved telescoping lemma supplies the all-depth transfer bound needed by the ramified-prime route, up to a constant transient. Falsification is a P^2 class with P^3 lifts having different successors, any omitted signed/DROP/internal-kernel state, or a reachable cycle whose gain prevents a 1/4-rate potential certificate.
